paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Micah had just said Jerusalem's mountain would be plowed like a field (Micah 3:12), and then he looks to the last days and says the LORD's mountain will be raised above the hills (Micah 4:1). The ruin was not the last word. God has the last word, and He keeps it.

Look at what the nations come for. They say, "He will teach us His ways, so that we may walk in His paths" (Micah 4:2). They don't come to be handed a prize. They come to be taught, and when the LORD settles things between them, the swords become plowshares and nobody trains for war anymore (Micah 4:3). The people sitting under their own vine and fig tree have "no one to frighten" them, and Micah says why you can count on it: "the mouth of the LORD of Hosts has spoken" (Micah 4:4).

And now the part that gets me RIGHT in the apron. The LORD says, "I will gather the lame; I will assemble the outcast," and He makes them a strong nation (Micah 4:6-7). I know what it's like to be shoved to the back and written off. Baker, if you feel forgotten, hear this: the LORD gathers the ones everybody else left behind, and He is the One who rules over them forever. So keep walking in His name and let His Word teach you His ways (Micah 4:5).
